knowledge:
- key_parameters: ynames=Character vector of target metabolite column names ;; mxtrModel=Formula of the form ~ x1+x2...|z1+z2... where x's model presence/absence (discrete portion) and z's model the mean of observed values (continuous portion) ;; fullModel=In mxtrmod, specifying the full model formula when running a reduced model ensures both models are fit on the same set of observations if covariates have missing values ;; adj=In mxtrmodLRT, the multiple testing adjustment method (e.g., "BH") ;; batchTvals=In mixnorm, a numeric vector of batch-specific thresholds of detectability; if omitted, defaults to the minimum observed abundance for each batch across all target metabolites ;; qc.sd.outliers=In mixnorm, the standard deviation threshold to exclude outlying quality control samples from batch effect estimation (defaults to 2) ;; removeCorrection=In mixnorm, a character vector of covariates to include in the mixture model for estimation but preserve (not subtract) in the final normalized data
- alternatives: Complete case analysis, imputation, and classic dimension reduction tools adapted for missing data are mentioned as common but less elegant alternatives to mixture modeling.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing or normalizing non-targeted metabolomics data (or other truncated/left-censored data) where a substantial portion of values are missing due to being below the threshold of detectability, and both presence/absence and abundance levels are biologically meaningful.
- pitfalls: Failing to specify the fullModel parameter when running reduced models in mxtrmod, which can lead to full and reduced models being fit on different subsets of observations if covariates have missing values ;; Missing values in the mixture model covariates themselves, which will cause the functions to fail ;; Completely missing quality control data for a batch or phenotype level, which prevents estimation of those effects and results in NA estimates, Inf normalized values, or failure to output data ;; Running mixnorm on a subset of metabolites without manually specifying batchTvals, which can lead to inconsistent normalization results because the default threshold depends on the minimum of the input subset.

workflows.name: mixture_model_association_analysis
workflows.intent: Run mixture model association analysis on metabolites with missing values to test for significant differences between phenotype groups while controlling for covariates.
input: experimental_metabolite_data.csv (Data frame, matrix, or ExpressionSet containing log-transformed metabolite levels with missing values as NA, along with phenotype and covariate columns)
workflows.stages:
1. Define target metabolite names and set the reference level for categorical predictors.
2. Specify the full and reduced mixture model formulas.
3. Fit the full mixture model using mxtrmod.
4. Fit the reduced mixture model using mxtrmod, specifying the fullModel parameter to maintain consistent observations.
5. Perform nested likelihood ratio tests using mxtrmodLRT.
6. Calculate estimated presence proportions and mean differences for reporting.

workflows.name: mixture_model_normalization
workflows.intent: Normalize batch and technical effects in experimental metabolomics data using repeated control/QC samples while accounting for batch-specific thresholds of detectability.
input: experimental_samples.csv (Data frame, matrix, or ExpressionSet containing raw experimental metabolite abundances and batch/phenotype covariates)
control_samples.csv (Data frame, matrix, or ExpressionSet containing raw quality control pool metabolite abundances, batch, and run order/phenotype covariates)
workflows.stages:
1. Define target metabolite names.
2. Run mixture model normalization using mixnorm, specifying batch-specific thresholds and outlier criteria.
3. (Optional) Run normalization preserving biological covariates (e.g., phenotype) using the removeCorrection parameter.
4. Assess normalization performance and identify outliers using metabplot.
workflows.code:
library(metabomxtr)
data(euMetabData)
data(euMetabCData)
ynames<-c('pyruvic_acid','malonic_acid')
euMetabNorm <- mixnorm(ynames, batch="batch", mxtrModel=~pheno+batch|pheno+batch, 
				batchTvals=c(10.76,11.51,11.36,10.31,11.90), cData=euMetabCData,
				data=euMetabData, qc.sd.outliers=2)
plot.list<-lapply(ynames, metabplot, batch="batch", raw.obs.data=euMetabData, raw.cont.data=euMetabCData, 
			norm.obs.data=euMetabNorm$obsNorm, norm.cont.data=euMetabNorm$ctlNorm,
			 color.var="pheno", cont.outlier.sd.thresh=2, norm.outlier.sd.thresh=4)
euMetabNormRC <- mixnorm(ynames, batch="batch", mxtrModel=~pheno+batch|pheno+batch, 
				batchTvals=c(10.76,11.51,11.36,10.31,11.90), cData=euMetabCData,
				removeCorrection="pheno",data=euMetabData)
metabplot("pyruvic_acid",  batch="batch", raw.obs.data=euMetabData, raw.cont.data=euMetabCData, 
		norm.obs.data=euMetabNormRC$obsNorm, norm.cont.data=euMetabNormRC$ctlNorm, 
		color.var="pheno", cont.outlier.sd.thresh=2, norm.outlier.sd.thresh=4)
